english: look for a needle in a haystack
also: to look for a needle in a haystack

terms.comment: Traupman gives it for a needle in a haystack. Lewis & Short explains the proverb as finding difficulties where there are none (Ennius; see that record), but in Plautus a slave says it of a search he thinks hopeless, adding “why don’t we go home, unless we mean to write a history?” (in scirpō nōdum quaeris: quīn nōs hinc domum redīmus, nisi sī historiam scrīptūrī sumus?, Men. 2.1.22–23, Lewis & Short s.vv. nōdus, historia): a search for what is not there. We have found no classical phrase for a search for something that is there but hard to find.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency.
Lewis & Short: nodus · Lewis & Short: historia
